div.l: And when þis good man saw it was soo
As he þat wise was and obedient
To kepe þe forward bi his fre assent
And seide Furst y schal . begyn þe game
Welcome be þe Cutt in goddes name
Now lete vs ride and herkenyth what y sey
And wᵗith þat worde we redyn forth on oure wey
And he began wᵗith right a mery chere
His tale anon / and seide on þis manere //

¶ Iam que domos Patrias · scithice post asꝑpera gentes
Prelia · laurigero ⁊etc̉etera
Whilom as olde stories tellen vs
Ther was a Duke þat hight Theseus
Of Athenes he was lorde and goủernour
And in his tyme suche a Conquerour
Þat gretter was þer noon vnder þe son̄
Ful many a riche Contre had he won̄
What with his wisdom and his Chiualrye
He conquered al þe londe of Femenye
That whilom was called Cythea
And wedded þe quene eke ypolita
And browth here home to his Contre
Wᵗith moche glorye and eke grete solempnite
And eke here yonger Suster Emelye
And þus with Victory and melodye
Lete y þis noble Duke to Athenes ride
And all his oost in armes hym beside
But certes if it were not to long̉e to here
Y wolde haue tolde you fully þe manere
How wonne was the regne of Femenye
By Theseus and his noble Chiualrye
And of þe grete bataile for þe nones
Betwix Athenes and Amasones
And how beseged was ypolita
Þe faire hardy quene of Cithea
And of þe fest þat was att here weddyng
And of þe tempest att here home comyng
But al þis as now y mote forbere
I haue god wote a large feeld to eere
And weke be myn oxen in my plowgh
Þe remanent of my tale is long y nowgh
This Duke of whom y make mencyon
When he was almost come to þe Toun̄
In al his wele and his moste pride
He was ware as he cast his eye aside
Wher þat þer kneled in þe hygh wey
A Companye of ladies twey and twey
Eche after oþer in clothes blake
But soche a crye ⁊and such a wo þei dede make
Þat in þis wordil is no Creature leuyng͗e
Þat herde soche a nodir weymentyng͗e
